catalog_quote: 3.2.8 Stress. Stress, the relative degree of intensity with which the syllables of an Abu' word are spoken, is characterized in three different ways. An unmarked syllable has the weakest stress in the word, the strongest stress is marked with a " ´ ". Secondary (or intermediate) level of stress is marked by " ` ". Words of one syllable show no stress mark since there is no other stress level to which the syllable of monosyllabic words is compared. The following seems to be the pattern of rules governing stress. The first vowel of diphthong of bi- or poly-syllabic words receives primary stress (diphthongs override vowels). Once that is established, the secondary and the weakest stress is decided. new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Abu' (catalog-all-2026-09-12) has an empty rule and there are no existing stress statements, so this source supplies the placement rather than agreeing or disagreeing with one: fixed initial stress, non-phonemic, no tone. The description is of the Southern dialect of Abu' spoken in Womsis village (the author's own dialect).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is predictable and non-contrastive: it falls on the first syllable of the word (rule /'V-, i.e. stress the initial vowel), illustrated by ['kwafita] 'spoon', ['dabah] 'finger', ['ʔutam] 'stone'. Neither stress nor tone is phonemic. Word-final vowels are half-long, which is a separate length rule, not a stress cue.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. The paper is a sketch of nominal concord; the phonology (§1.4) is a short preliminary, so the stress rule is asserted, not argued, and no polysyllabic exceptions or loanword cases are discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Nekitel 1986 describes Abu' as spoken by about 300 people in Womsis village, ~70 km west of Wewak (West Sepik / Sandaun Province), and specifically the Southern of the two Abu' dialects spoken there, since the author is a native speaker of it (§1.3, p. 179). Note 2 (p. 204) says earlier literature (Laycock 1973, 1975) treated Abu' as a dialect of Mountain Arapesh, whereas Nekitel regards it as a distinct language of the Arapesh family spoken in Aspeis, Balup, Malin, Walihiga, Womsis, Amom, Womsak No. 1 and Womsak No. 2. This matches Glottolog abua1245 Abu' (Nuclear Torricelli), not Mountain Arapesh (Bukiyip).

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage is verbatim on thesis pp. 53-54 (PDF 67-68) of the Nekitel 1985 PDF we hold; locator and the 3.2.9 tone contrast are correct. (2) The deciding source is the only grammar-level description of Abu' (Glottolog's sole 'grammar', by a native-speaker linguist trained at ANU); no phonology article, JIPA illustration or instrumental study surfaced in Glottolog 5.1's bib, arapesh.org's bibliography, or OpenLibrary, and none is cited anywhere in the works opened. sources.note: Same author's published phonology summary states plain word-initial stress with no diphthong override (and transcribes ['nõmboil] with initial stress); worth citing alongside the thesis as corroboration of the initial default and as evidence that the CVV clause is the thesis's hedged addition.
